title: The Bioprocess Brief
interests: Bioprocess development, process intensification, scale-up, perfusion, media optimization, and process analytics
Mammalian cell engineering, especially Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cell line development and recombinant protein production
Metabolic engineering, flux analysis, and systems biology with a clear application to industrial biotechnology or mammalian cells
Cell and gene therapy manufacturing, viral vector production, engineered therapeutic cells, and enabling platform technologies

The mechanistic link from nuclear respiratory factor 1 (NRF1)-driven mitochondrial biogenesis and energy metabolism through AXER/SLC35B1-mediated endoplasmic reticulum ATP supply to CHO secretory capacity and recombinant protein productivity, including energy/redox engineering and biosensors. Distinguish nuclear respiratory factor 1 from the NFE2L1 alias NRF1, and GABPA (nuclear respiratory factor 2 in mitochondrial literature) from NFE2L2/NRF2; flag ambiguous gene identities rather than assuming equivalence.
